text: Baseline (local-full, full precision, n=200, seed 1): the checkpoint does NOT perform the behaviour. Top-1 accuracy against the dataset answers is 0.055 (below uniform chance over the 11-token vocab, 0.091). Mean logit diff correct-minus-incorrect is 0.015 +/- 0.28 on clean and -0.020 on corrupt, i.e. indistinguishable from zero and from each other. Example predictions are the input symbol 'ne', never an output symbol D/E/M. Pre-registered prediction (accuracy >= 0.9) REFUTED. The hypothesis 'the model reproduces the dataset answers' is rejected. Side note, not a claim about the model: the seed-0 dataset labels (E0001) fit 'more ka than se -> M, more se than ka -> E, tie -> D' on 63/64 examples by hand inspection, but this checkpoint does not compute those labels, so there is no mechanism to localise.

Stop after baseline per protocol step 1: accuracy is at/below chance, so there is no behaviour to explain. No circuit search, no verify_hypothesis (any 'circuit' found from here would be fit to noise). Report as a null finding with 2 of 25 experiments used.
